title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 2 | Week 4 vs. New York Giants
headline: LaFleur praised Elijah Higgins's blocking and receiving and said his best days are ahead; two injured players' return timelines remain undetermined, with no set date.
summary: LaFleur said Arizona runs a pure progression offense, so the quarterback's read order decides targets regardless of which receiver is involved. He praised Giants defender Javon Hollins, whose ball-hawking and playmaking he flagged as a concern, and said all of Arizona's players are aware of the threat. He described the league's challenge and penalty-clarification process as tricky, since teams can't always tell which calls the league would uphold, so he's selective about what he shows the team. On the rookie-style running question, he called his runner physical and said the goal is getting him down, without elaborating on penalty lines. He said yards-after-catch skill is a trained skill and credited Arizona's ball-security and closing-space work against the Chargers, while calling Seattle's tacklers better. He dismissed rain concerns for MetLife Stadium, saying it rains there every Sunday. Asked about two injured players, he said he doesn't check daily, leaves timelines to the medical staff, and will have more information when a return gets close; both players are returning on a return-to-performance basis. He said Elijah Higgins has become a physical blocker and a strong receiver, calling him a locomotive once he gets going. Finally, he said the team uses analytics for outside perspective on how opponents view the offense, but is not overly focused on small-sample data yet.

injuries.detail: Two players (names not clearly captured in the transcript) are working back; LaFleur said medical staff controls timing and he has no set return date.

signals.claim: Higgins's blocking and receiving have improved, and he is expected to keep a strong role in the tight end room.
signals.note: Praise for physical blocking and receiving suggests a growing, featured role in Arizona's offense.
signals.quote: I think his best days are ahead of him.

title: Jesse Minter Optimistic About Trey Hendrickson's Recovery Timeline
headline: Trey Hendrickson is out this week after a finger procedure, opening more pass-rush snaps for Ethan Burke and others; Lamar Jackson is getting normal reps.
summary: Minter announced that Trey Hendrickson will miss this week's home game after a finger procedure, which he expects to be short-term and which he believes will help Hendrickson long-term. He said the absence creates opportunity for other pass rushers, and he floated that Ethan Burke could see some defensive snaps for the first time. Minter called Carson Vinson much improved in his first start, praising his run and pass play and the lack of sacks allowed. He said Andrew Vorhees, a full-time starter last year, has had a strong camp and may see more opportunity this game. Minter was positive that Ronnie Stanley had two good practice days Wednesday and Thursday, though he will keep monitoring how Stanley feels through Friday and Saturday. He said Lamar Jackson has had his normal workload since Wednesday's practice and he is excited about Sunday. On the upcoming opponent's dominant defensive tackle, Minter said the offense has a plan with different looks and that it will come down to playing down by down. He also discussed a rookie playing a new position who has handled the added responsibility well, though the player is not identified clearly in the captions.

He said the staff will keep evaluating through game day, with a final decision made after waking up on game day and moving around, in a joint call with the medical staff and the player. T.J. Sanders is listed as doubtful while he works back from an appendectomy, and Brady was encouraged by his mentality and by seeing him move on the practice field. Ray Davis is questionable after being limited the last couple of days. Brady said Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun are getting the same reps as before, so they are ready to step in for Benford. title: Dave Canales shares final updates before Sunday night against the Lions
headline: Jalen Coker (limited) and Monroe Freeling (protocol) are still uncertain for Sunday night vs. Detroit; John Metchie III is ready if Coker sits, and Xavier Legette is expected to miss the game.
summary: Canales opened by praising banged-up players who have worked their way back through a tough injury week, and said several are still progressing toward availability. Jalen Coker was brought out before practice for an individual period and got into some team periods, but he is listed as limited, and the staff will re-evaluate him again before game day. If Coker can't go, Canales said John Metchie III is practiced and ready, and David Moore has been catching punts. On the offensive line, Canales would not specify combinations if Monroe Freeling is out, though he confirmed Stone Forsythe is still in the mix. Freeling is in the concussion protocol, was cleared to fully participate in practice, and still has some steps to pass before he is cleared for contact. Xavier Legette is out this week, and Canales said he hopes to get him back quickly. On defense, Canales said Robert Rochelle and Corey Thornton were brought in to fill the cornerback depth and special teams roles, and that Chau Smith-Wade is expected to step up, with Will Lee offering nickel flexibility. Canales also discussed the forecast for a rainy game, which he expects to lean on the run game, and said the team is monitoring it with weather staff.

title: Ben Johnson on QBs: 'We have guys we believe in' | Press Conference
headline: Caleb Williams is out this week, so Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent are competing to start; Ozzy Trapilo is back in pads, and Dillon Thieneman is earning a bigger role at safety.
summary: Ben Johnson declined to name his Sunday starter and said he is comfortable with either quarterback, Case Keenum or Tyson Bagent, calling the room supportive and well prepared. Johnson said the staff is split when each coach is asked individually, and that the 'hot hand' factors into the decision alongside the longer body of work. The transcript is garbled on Caleb Williams, but the exchange reads as Williams being out this week. Running back D'Andre Swift is on the injury report with lingering effects from Monday Night Football, but Johnson expects him to practice and is optimistic for Sunday. Left tackle Ozzy Trapilo ('OSI' in the captions) is progressing well in pads and could return sooner rather than later, but Theo Benedet starts at left tackle this week. Colston Loveland is playing well and is trusted in the run game, but he has been used as a blocker more than Johnson wants, and the staff is working to get him more involved in the passing game. On defense, Johnson praised Dillon Thieneman's instincts and versatility at safety, noting he plays post, quarters, and blitzes and is always around the ball. Johnson also previewed the Jets, praising their edge rusher David Bailey and their tight end and noting that Garrett Wilson must be tracked on every play.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference: October 2nd, 2026
headline: Mason Graham's knee injury status is unclear with a possible MRI, while Deshaun Watson's growing confidence and Denzel Boston's early role point to continued offensive upside.
summary: Monken said he had no update on Mason Graham's knee injury and didn't know whether he was having an MRI, calling it a shame and hoping for good news. He praised Graham's effort, intelligence, and quickness despite his four sacks in three games. On Deshaun Watson, Monken said better protection, a stronger run game, and more stacked plays had given the quarterback confidence to push the ball downfield, and he expects continued improvement. He said the team still has penalty problems, with 43 accepted through four games and pre-snap penalties being the main thing it controls. Monken said Michael Hall returned from an ankle injury and Adin Huntington played heavy snaps on the interior, with the next-man-up mindset guiding the defense. He credited Denzel Boston's toughness and mindset, noting the team had tried to target him early, and said he will keep improving. On the late-game sequence, Monken said Watson's ball security is a point of emphasis, and he defended the quarterback's read while disappointed by the giveaways. He also talked about the team's resiliency in the win over a Rodgers-led opponent, saying the team must put opponents away early.

title: Brian Schottenheimer on 105.3 The Fan | 10-02-26
headline: Joey Porter Jr. is a Week 4 availability watch after the trade, while Javonte Williams and CeeDee Lamb are being leaned on more in the offense.
summary: Schottenheimer said acquiring Joey Porter Jr. was about winning now, pointing to Dak Prescott's play and a secondary that is badly banged up. He described Porter as a tall, physical press corner who can also run and chase, and said he fits the scheme's match-principle zones. Porter had a strong first day in the building, but the coach said Sunday's status depends on how he moves and whether he is sore the next day. Schottenheimer took responsibility for the Baltimore loss, saying he did not finish well and that a better third-down call might have won it. He defended the fade route, calling it a high-percentage shot with elite receivers like CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. He praised Javonte Williams's play and said the run game was strong enough to keep him calling runs in the opening drive. On Houston, he said the 0-3 record understates a talented roster, with Nico Collins expected back and David Montgomery added to the backfield.

title: HC Sean Payton on facing the 49ers: ‘It’s a well-coached team’
headline: Payton calls the 49ers a well-coached team, praises Mike McGlinchey and Quinn Meinerz, and reports no new Denver injury news.
summary: Payton previewed Sunday's game against the 49ers, noting the heat forecast of about 92 degrees and that the team has contingency plans in place. He reflected on the 20th anniversary of the Saints' 2006 return to the Superdome, recalling the long training camp in Jackson, Mississippi and how emotional that season was. He praised Quinn Meinerz's rare athleticism, work ethic, and toughness, and said his passion is contagious. He explained that signing Mike McGlinchey filled a clear need at right tackle, calling him smart, tough, and dependable week to week. He described DJ Jones as a respected leader and an important part of the team's fabric. On the 49ers, he said Fred Warner is the centerpiece of their defense, that their red zone defense has been strong, and that Raheem Morris's group is well coached and full of problems. He also said that interior pressure on quarterbacks reflects a well-coached defensive line.

title: Campbell on SNF vs. Carolina Panthers
headline: Brian Branch is close to returning and Jack Campbell is 'just fine' per Campbell, while D.J. Wonnum is emerging opposite Hutchinson ahead of SNF at Carolina.
summary: Campbell said the Lions are fully prepared for a loud, prime-time environment in Carolina, pointing to Bryce Young's scrambling and the Panthers' versatile run game and tight ends as the main threats. He downplayed any extra motivation from the 2022 loss there, calling it a different coaching staff and roster. On the defensive line, he said the key is to push the pocket inside and contain Young without letting him escape the edges. He said Brian Branch is close to returning and is ready to go, and that timelines have shifted. Campbell praised D.J. Wonnum's consistency and said he is starting to win his own reps opposite Aidan Hutchinson, which opens up the interior. He said Jack Campbell is fine, is still the team's bell cow, and is not losing confidence despite his public comments. On young players, Campbell said Jackson Meeks is still raw at tight end but growing, and that his value currently comes mostly from special teams, with more offensive snaps as he develops. He said Jimmy Rolder has shown well on special teams and that the staff would like to mix him into defense at some point. Asked about the secondary, Campbell said the front office is always looking to upgrade and will add help if the value and fit are right, and that the team was involved in a recent trade pursuit.

title: Matt LaFleur pleased with the step Matthew Golden has taken in Year 2
headline: LaFleur praised Matthew Golden's physical growth in Year 2, while an unnamed offensive lineman suffered a significant injury and Aaron Banks is still working through an issue.

He described the week as unusual because the line is getting about three new bodies, and said the newcomers have made a positive impact. Kevin Zeitler, who had no training camp or offseason, is working his way back and gaining comfort daily, and LaFleur noted he has a lot of practice reps. The coach said Zeitler has been stationed beside the line during some drills to sharpen focus through mental reps. Aaron Banks is doing rehab work on the side, and LaFleur said he is just working through it with no clear timeline. A lineman, whose name was garbled in the transcript, went down after slipping and is expected to miss a significant amount of time, with the injury largely non-contact. LaFleur said the depth room has been thinner since then and the remaining players will carry more load. On the heat expected Sunday around 90 degrees, he stressed hydration and nutrition, which the team has been emphasizing all week. On the passing game, he said Golden and Christian Watson have started strong, but the tight ends and backs need to be more involved. He praised Golden for separation and for the physicality the team challenged him on last year, including fighting for extra yards in both the run and pass game.

title: Shane Steichen: Week 4 final update, Colts vs. Commanders
headline: No Colts player ruled out for Week 4 in London; Ashton Dulin is back at practice after a few weeks away, and Mo Alie-Cox (illness) has progressed but is still uncertain.
summary: Steichen opened by saying the Colts have not ruled anyone out for Sunday's game against Washington and praised the travel and hotel setup for the London trip. He described the Commanders' starting quarterback, transcribed as Marcus, as a veteran who is mobile, can make plays with his legs, and is effective in the pocket, so Indianapolis must win the rush lanes and play strong back-end coverage. He framed the trip as a business trip where the focus is staying locked in despite possible distractions, noting the team flew a red-eye Thursday night and will hold a mock game before Sunday. On body clock, he said the staff is keeping players on their Indianapolis schedule, with late nights and sleep-ins, and that sports performance staff is handling checks and reminders. He called the win over Seattle, where the Colts lost the turnover battle 3-0 but rallied late, a sign of resilience. On late-game decisions, he said clock management is a big part of close games and that finishing with a kick or a touchdown with no time left is the goal. On injuries, he said Ashton Dulin had his first practice in a couple of weeks, and that Mo Alie-Cox, still dealing with illness, progressed well on the trip and is in a good spot, though the team will see how he is on Sunday.

title: Liam Coen on Final Preparations for Bengals, Practicing the Right Way | Press Conference
headline: Coen praised Brian Thomas Jr.'s week and Bhayshul Tuten's efficiency, and said both need to keep producing as Jacksonville prepares for Cincinnati.
summary: Coen said the week of prep went well, with a physical practice Thursday and special teams period he called one of the best of his tenure. He described Brian Thomas Jr. as having a great week, noting a strong practice with Trevor Lawrence and saying the team will need him and the other perimeter players to keep making plays. He said Bryan Thomas Jr. has earned trust through production, citing his get-off and effort against the run in limited rush opportunities against New England. Coen praised Bhayshul Tuten's discipline and efficiency, including yards after contact, while acknowledging the team has not yet seen many long runs from him, and said the staff wants to create cleaner lanes for his speed. He spoke about road game communication challenges and how the staff limits in-game calls on the road. On the Patriots game, he explained that heavy zone looks forced situational play-call changes on the headset and sideline. He said the staff calls plays not practiced during the week maybe five to ten times since he arrived, and that core concepts give them flexible answers. He framed Cincinnati's offense as dangerous because of Chase Brown's versatility as a back and receiver, along with Burrow and Chase, and he praised Travis Hunter's accountability after his pass interference penalty.

title: Sean McVay speaks on special teams updates, keys to beating the Eagles, Puka Nacua's return & more
headline: Puka Nacua is good to go and looked sharp in Thursday's heavy workload, while Xavier Smith lost punt return duties to a new group that Alex Bachman leads, and Aaron Donald is out with soreness.
summary: McVay opened with injury news: Colby Parkinson is questionable, Terrance Ferguson and Jaylen Watson are out, Aaron Donald is out, and a Stewart (likely Josaiah) is dealing with a groin injury. On Donald, McVay said he has soreness that did not improve after Sunday's game, and that sitting him was a protective decision made with Reggie. He rejected the idea that Donald's per-game bonuses factored in. On special teams, McVay said Xavier Smith is being replaced because the unit needs better production and ball security, not because of a lack of respect for Smith. Alex Bachman is the immediate candidate to take over that role, and McVay is wary of using starting running back Kyren Williams there. He said the team will keep looking at outside options. McVay called the schedule and injuries a test, acknowledged the losses, and framed the week as a chance to grow. For Puka Nacua, McVay said he is good to go, looks explosive and strong, and handled a heavy Thursday workload well, though snap count management remains a consideration. Myles Garrett is progressing in rehab with no timeline yet. McVay also named Curt Sandoval a Crucial Catch captain. The Eagles game is this Sunday.

O'Connell said the week of preparation without Jefferson has helped the rest of the group, since younger players like Tai Felton and Myles Price got their first run-through of the game plan. title: WATCH: McCarthy on the loss to the Browns
headline: Pittsburgh's offense and defense both faltered in the 27-24 loss to Cleveland; McCarthy gave no injury updates and little fantasy-specific detail, and cornerback depth is a watch item after the trade of Joey (not on the roster list).
summary: McCarthy said the first drive was hectic and about 20 plays, and that communication settled in afterward. He acknowledged that some of Aaron Rodgers' sideline exchanges got heated and said he wished he had chosen his words differently. He credited Cleveland's aggressive five-man, man-to-man pressure for the protection problems, saying the game was herky-jerky and decided by who made the big play. He said the team made mistakes in all three phases and was most disappointed in situational football, given how much time the staff puts into it. He also said Cleveland spread the ball well with a balanced attack, and he admitted the team missed too many tackles. He said the trade of Joey was a business decision made the day before the game, that the team had been working toward a possible return for him, and that he wished him well in Dallas. On the Boswell missed field goal and the reversed pass-interference call, he had no evaluation of the kick and explained that the defensive coaches believed Jack tipped the ball, which led him to throw the flag.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Gives Final Updates Ahead Of Week 4 vs. Chargers
headline: Jadarian Price is out with a re-aggravated chest injury, leaving Zach Charbonnet, George Holani, and Velus Jones Jr. as the next backfield options; Charbonnet is practicing but has no return timeline.
summary: Macdonald called it a business-as-usual week after a strong Friday practice, with the process continuing until kickoff. He said Jadarian Price is out after re-aggravating a chest injury on Wednesday, and that the injury is not Price's fault. Ty Okada is questionable, and Chazz Surratt is also questionable with a chest re-aggravation from Wednesday practice; Macdonald did not yet know whether it is a longer-term concern. He said the team has ready backups behind Price who are preparing hard. Zach Charbonnet practiced this week after sitting out last week, and Macdonald said he looks fantastic, but he declined to project a return date and said the process must be respected. Macdonald praised George Holani's handling of checkdowns in the passing game against Washington and called Brady Russell the engine of the core special teams unit, with fullback and tight end roles on offense. He also spoke about Velus Jones Jr., saying he has been great at gunner and is ready if an opportunity comes in the backfield, and he praised Leonard Williams as a world-class player.

title: Shanahan Talks Injuries, Purdy's Pocket Mobility, Previews Broncos
headline: Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams are out for Denver; Jaden Dugger (shoulder), Mike Evans, Dre Greenlaw and Keion White are questionable, with Dugger a game-time decision.
summary: Shanahan opened with injury news: Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams are out, while Mike Evans, Dre Greenlaw, Keion White and Jaden Dugger are questionable. Dugger's shoulder injury came from practice the day before, and Shanahan said he will be a game-time decision. He called the Broncos' quarterback keeper game an extremely important thing to defend and praised Brock Purdy's arm strength and mobility out of the pocket. He said Purdy is one of the best at escaping pressure, and that film study and drills with towels help him improve. Shanahan said Brandin Cooks has had a good two weeks learning the offense and is improving quickly. He said Jordan Watkins stood out in run blocking and on film, not just his two catches. He said the team's goal is to finish games and reach the playoffs, and that the opponent's record doesn't matter. He also said Dante Pettis hurt his calf in practice, and that a Christian Kirk calf injury will likely keep him out next week. He declined to react much to the league's suspension of Jed York, and he discussed leadership and how he approaches preparing for opponents.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Carnell Tate is trending up in the run game and route running, while Anthony Hill's role grows but his Mike-linebacker communication is still a work in progress; Kevin Winston is a questionable shoulder case.
summary: Saleh opened by noting that Kevin Winston appeared on the injury report after a fall on his shoulder, but he is not overly concerned and will see how Winston feels at practice; everyone else is good to go. He said the offensive line has a couple of players working through hurdles, that the right guard situation is comfortable and that the group has worked well, and he praised the center for communication and said the right guard is playing at a Pro Bowl level. On the slow starts, Saleh said the team is in the fourth game of its first quarter of the season and blamed execution in critical situations, especially third downs, drops, mistimed throws, and a special teams turnover to open a game, rather than play-calling or tempo. He said the team has to master the obvious and do the little things better. Ahead of a matchup with a dual-threat quarterback and a bruising running back, Saleh said there is no way to simulate Lamar Jackson, so the team is focused on rush lanes, discipline, edge setting, and coverage. On Carnell Tate, Saleh praised his run blocking and steady route-running growth, though he acknowledged the workload dynamic with a veteran receiver who had been starting. On the linebackers, Saleh said the group of Anthony Hill, Cody Barton, James Williams and another player is strong enough that all should play significant snaps, and he said Hill's length, speed and range stand out, though his post-snap communication as the Mike still needs major growth.
